Hi everyone,

I'm halfway through 'Roadside Picnic' and I thought I'd share some spoiler-friendly observations...

  • this book is strong on the concept of alien. The aliens have interacted with earth, and there are examples of alien phenomena and equipment... but the earth-people are quite clued-out about it. They have no real idea how the phenomena work or the physical principles behind them; about the aliens, who they are or where they came from or went on to. The true mystery of the situation is profound, and so far no explanations are offered whatsoever. And it's not frustrating, it's intriguing. It's real SF, for sure. The humans are interacting with things that are far beyond their understanding or comprehension.

  • you realize that the author indeed wrote this book in a police state. The main character's struggles against the law enforcement are a permanent feature of the events of the book. Many of these interactions, you can imagine, come from real-life examples of people being hauled in before the authorities, and confronted with this or that.

  • You also realize the authors are very Russian. The main character drinks heavily, smokes quite a lot, faces death repeatedly with courage (aided by a few shots of liquor), is tough and gets into fights and confrontations easily.

  • I'm trying to decide if the author is symbolically describing life in the USSR, or in the West, with the events of the book. The setting is not in the USSR, nor in Europe, but it's not clear where the town they are in, is situated (and I also am unsure if they are in the USA either, although that is hinted at in one scene). I'm suspecting so far that perhaps it's an amalgam of life in the USSR and (what the author thinks as) life in the West.

It's an enjoyable read, and I'm looking forward to the rest of the book.
Halfway through 'Roadside Picnic', and some thoughts...

... oh, and an extra comment: there is humor, too. There are incidents that are comical; one in particular had me laughing out loud. I won't spoil it (and you'd have to read the situation, and the context it lies within). But yes it gave me a good laugh.
